equity_bridge.item: Class A preferred shares at par (8 series, 74.972m x $25)
equity_bridge.note: Q2-2026 MD&A outstanding share data, line 1308-1315; unchanged from 20-Feb-2026

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (2.0-2.2%) diverges >30% from EPS and revenue CAGRs, but both of those are distorted: revenue by the FY2023 gross-to-net restatement (FY2022 11,611 was never restated, so the 3yr CAGR shows a false cliff) and commodity prices; EPS by the FY2022 one-off gain (5.12) and the FY2024 616m loss on acquisition. Equity growth is held down by a dividend payout above earnings. Adjusted EBITDA per share (3.0%) is the cleanest per-share operating series and was selected instead.
historical_growth.notes: FCF here = OCF - capex; SBC is cash-settled and already inside OCF, so reported and owner FCF coincide. The FY2020 base (capex-heavy, 1,223) flatters the 5yr FCF CAGR; the 3yr 2.7% is the more representative figure. Reported FCF excludes JV contributions (410 FY2025), which the model treats as capex.

scenario_narratives.base: Pembina remains the dominant WCSB liquids and gas-processing network: fee-based Pipelines and Facilities (~80%+ of Adjusted EBITDA) grow mid-single-digit on Montney/NEBC volumes and the Peace expansions; Marketing (499 in FY2025 vs 724 in FY2024) stays around its weaker recent level; Cedar LNG starts paying distributions from 2029 and Greenlight from 2031. The capex/contribution cycle peaks in 2026-29 and then tapers, lifting owner FCF materially in the back half. Cash taxes drift up toward statutory as tax pools are used.
scenario_narratives.bull: Montney drilling accelerates on LNG Canada Phase 2 and Canadian west-coast LNG exports; Pembina sanctions the Birch-to-Taylor and Taylor-to-Gordondale expansions and further PGI processing builds at attractive build multiples; Cedar LNG comes in on time and on budget with a second expansion option; GLEC's site expands toward its 1,864MW permit on further data-centre demand; NGL frac spreads and propane export margins support Marketing above 600. Higher growth capex is funded internally and the market keeps paying ~19x for long-lived contracted infrastructure.
scenario_narratives.bear: WCSB volume growth stalls (low gas prices, LNG ramp delays), Marketing margins compress further on narrow frac spreads, the Alliance new toll structure and contract re-pricing erode Pipelines revenue, and Cedar LNG suffers cost overruns or delay that raise contributions and defer distributions. Cash taxes reach statutory sooner. Federal emissions caps and transition policy compress the terminal multiple to 13x with ~1% perpetual growth. Leverage (~3.5x net debt / Adjusted EBITDA incl. hybrids, plus 3.9bn proportionate JV debt) limits flexibility but is not a solvency threat given investment-grade ratings and contracted cash flows.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Cash-basis owner-FCF DCF on a long-lived, mostly contracted midstream network. JVs are valued through their cash distributions with contributions charged as capex, so JV project debt is netted inside the flows rather than in the bridge. Preferred shares are a senior claim deducted at par. SBC is cash-settled and already in EBITDA, so house and street coincide. The valuation is terminal-heavy, as any long-duration infrastructure asset is; the cap multiple, not Gordon, binds in every scenario and encodes the energy-transition discount.
key_risks_to_valuation: Cedar LNG construction cost or schedule overrun (Pembina 49.9%, US$2bn net, in service late 2028)
WCSB volume growth slowdown or LNG Canada Phase 2 delay reduces expansion throughput
Marketing segment commodity exposure (NGL frac spreads, propane export margins)
Energy-transition policy (federal emissions cap) compressing the terminal multiple
Interest-rate sensitivity: ~13.2bn corporate debt plus ~3.9bn proportionate JV debt; 1.2bn current maturities at 30-Jun-2026

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 50.15-72.72

inputs.share_count_basis: Weighted-average diluted 582m, Q2-2026 MD&A (581.2m common + 2.0m options at 20-Feb-2026). Held FLAT: SBC is cash-settled and already inside EBITDA; no buybacks since FY2023, no equity issuance planned.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 cash flow statement: share-based compensation expense 94 accrued, 89 paid in cash (share-based compensation payment line). Pembina's awards are predominantly cash-settled; the expense is NOT added back in Adjusted EBITDA (no SBC line in the reconciliation, FY2025 AR line 3275-3297) and the cash payment is already deducted inside operating cash flow. It is therefore a real cash cost already inside the EBITDA margin and reported FCF, so sbc_incl_equity_taxes is 0 to avoid charging it twice and sbc_pct_path is 0 (SBC row kept explicit at 0%). Share count flat at ~581m since 2022 confirms no stock-settled dilution.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-09T20:00:00Z regular close (TSX), Yahoo Finance chart API
inputs.wacc_rationale: CAD build. Risk-free ~3.3% (GoC 10y), ERP 5.0%, beta ~1.0 -> cost of equity ~8.3-8.5%. Pre-tax cost of debt 4.5-5.3% (MTN 4.5%, hybrids 5.3%, Q2-26 MD&A) -> ~3.6% after 23% tax. Preferreds ~5.5%. Market weights: equity ~39.3bn (72%), debt 13.2bn (24%), prefs 1.9bn (4%) -> ~7.2%. Used 7.25% in all three scenarios; risk is charged in the scenario flows, not the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost: lease cash cost (FY2025 principal 84 + est. interest ~25 = ~109, 1.4% of revenue) deducted via lease_cost_pct_path; lease liabilities (594 at 30-Jun-2026: 82 current + 512 non-current) EXCLUDED from net debt. D&A path is ex right-of-use depreciation (987 reported less ~75 est. ROU = ~912, 11.7% of revenue).
inputs.nci_treatment: None. Pembina bought out the Aux Sable U.S. minority (Aug-2024, 220m); no NCI on the balance sheet at 30-Jun-2026.
inputs.equity_accounted_treatment: Pembina holds large JV interests (PGI 60%, Cedar LNG 49.9%, Greenlight 47.5%, others). The flows are CASH-BASIS: EBITDA = consolidated Adjusted EBITDA ex proportionate JV EBITDA (4,289 - (209 share of profit + 535 adjustments) = 3,545) PLUS cash distributions from JVs (544) = 4,089, 52.6% of FY2025 revenue. Contributions to JVs (410 FY2025; 331 H1-2026, Cedar LNG peak year; Greenlight up to ~1.0bn over 2028-30) sit inside the capex path. JV-level debt (Pembina share 3,862 at Dec-25, incl. Cedar construction loan) is therefore NOT added to net debt: distributions are already after JV debt service. Investments in equity accounted investees (4,469 book) are NOT added to the bridge -- their value is in the distribution stream.
inputs.notes: MODEL: Owner-FCF DCF with the non-US / capital-intensive adaptations (owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md). Routed as an operating company (midstream infrastructure: pipelines, gas processing, fractionation, marketing), not a REIT/bank/LIC. First valuation of PPL.TO; no prior DCF and no MEMORY.md entry. Analysis JSON was not yet written when this was built; narratives draw on the filings. FLOWS: unlevered, cash-basis JV treatment (see equity_accounted_treatment). Revenue is used as the scale driver only; Pembina's revenue swings with commodity prices in Marketing (FY2023 restated gross-to-net, 9,125 -> 6,331), so the growth path is effectively a cash-EBITDA growth path at a slowly rising margin. Sustaining capex is small (210 non-recoverable guided for 2026); the capex path is mostly growth capex and JV contributions, which is what funds the EBITDA growth. 2026 capex guidance ~940 (FY2025 AR line 1424) plus ~650 JV contributions. EQUITY BRIDGE: net debt 13,060 = loans and borrowings 12,191 (1,200 current + 10,991 non-current) + subordinated hybrid notes 1,022 - cash 153, all 30-Jun-2026; then preferred shares deducted at par (74.972m shares x $25 = 1,874), since preferred dividends (~120-134/yr) are not in the flows. Leases treatment (B). Decommissioning provision (527) and finance-lease receivables (210) left out as roughly offsetting long-dated items. BUYBACKS: none since FY2023 (50 in FY2023, 333 in FY2022); the flat count is not being funded by repurchases but SBC is cash-settled so there is no grant dilution to fund. SBC-ZERO treatment: house and street coincide (band_position null) because SBC is cash, not because it is absent.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +2.5%: H1-2026 Adjusted EBITDA 2,195 vs 2,180 in H1-2025, i.e. flat, with Marketing still soft. 2027-28 +4%: NEBC/Peace expansions (RFS IV, Fox Creek-to-Namao, Birch-to-Taylor, Taylor-to-Gordondale) and PGI growth. 2029 +5% plus margin step: Cedar LNG in service late 2028 (US$2bn net, take-or-pay), distributions start after project debt service. 2030-31: Greenlight (GLEC, 932MW, in service H2-2030) distributions. Cash EBITDA CAGR ~4.4% over 10 years, in line with the 4.6% 3yr Adjusted EBITDA CAGR and mid-single-digit fee-based growth.
base.capex_rationale: 2026: ~940 capex guidance + ~650 JV contributions (331 in H1, Cedar's largest year). 2027-29 stays elevated for the Peace expansions and up to ~1.0bn of Greenlight equity over 2028-30. Tapers to ~11.5% of revenue (slightly above D&A) once the project cycle ends, enough to fund 2% terminal growth.
base.tax_rationale: Unlevered cash tax on EBIT. FY2025: taxes paid 346 + interest shield ~137 = ~483 on cash EBIT ~3,069 = 15.7%; current tax expense 432 implies ~18.5%. Ramps toward the ~23% Alberta/federal combined statutory rate, held at 22% for ongoing CCA on growth capex.
base.terminal_rationale: Gordon at 7.25%/2.0% is ~19.4x; capped at 17x for energy-transition terminal risk on hydrocarbon throughput.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 17x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 20% (above the 15% default): leverage including JV project debt is meaningful, and both the Cedar LNG construction risk and Marketing commodity exposure are live in 2026-28. Base 55%: ~80% of EBITDA is fee-based under long-term take-or-pay and cost-of-service contracts, which narrows the outcome range. Bull 25% (below the 35% default): it needs several independent things -- new FIDs, LNG Phase 2, stronger frac spreads and a re-rated terminal multiple -- to all go right.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
